subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Lu Yu: The Sage of Tea
description: A quick, practical guide to Lu Yu: The Sage of Tea.

hook.text: Lu Yu wrote 'The Classic of Tea' around 760 CE—the world's first book entirely about tea. It transformed tea from drink to art.

buildup.text: Orphaned as a child and raised in a Buddhist monastery, Lu Yu spent decades studying tea cultivation and preparation.

discovery.text: His book covered water quality, utensils, leaf grades, correct boiling, and even the spiritual state of the brewer.

twist.text: After his death, Lu Yu was deified. Tea merchants placed his statue in their shops—pouring tea over it for luck.

climax.text: Lu Yu's work codified tea culture for 1,200+ years. Chinese, Japanese, and Korean tea traditions all reference his text.

punchline.text: One orphan, one book, twelve centuries of influence. Lu Yu made tea sacred.

quiz.question: What did Lu Yu write?
options: 'The Classic of Tea' — the first book entirely about tea, around 760 CE
